Years ago, friends in New York introduced me to TMPL Hell’s Kitchen, and it has remained one of the most memorable gyms I have trained in.

The atmosphere reminds me of other lively, LGBTQIA+ friendly spaces where people are there to work hard, enjoy themselves, and make everyone feel welcome. The lighting is fun without feeling gimmicky, the equipment is clean and well maintained, and the entire gym has an energy that makes it easy to look forward to your next workout.

I have spent enough time around gyms and coaches over the years to appreciate the difference between someone who simply works as a trainer and someone who genuinely understands fitness. After getting to know Dena, it was clear that she falls into the latter category. Her knowledge, discipline, and enthusiasm make her a great example of the kind of trainers available at TMPL.

If all you want is to pick up some weights and leave, there are plenty of gyms that can offer that. If you want music, lights, good equipment, and genuinely happy people who make the hard parts of training feel a little easier, TMPL is absolutely worth considering.

Initially I was put off by the the fact that each section has a screen showing you what exercise to do with the equipment, because I had previously only done classes with live instructors, but because there is always at least one coach walking around the gym, there is someone to show you what to do and help you if the video isn't clear enough. The screen shows the exercises continuously, so you don't lose your chance to figure out what to do either, whereas some live instructors will only show you a brief demo and then you're stuck looking around at other people to try to figure it out. By the end of my first class, I was very impressed with the efficiency Sweat440's system.

The coaches are all extremely nice and helpful, and the environment is very welcoming. Especially Jorge, Ronnie, and Daniel, who always help me out and encourage me to step it up if it looks like I need more of a challenge. While I often see a lot of the same people in classes, I like that you can talk to people if you want to but there's no pressure to be social if you just want to work out.

My biggest concern is the climbing program. Reduced staffing appeared to coincide with a decline in supervision and training opportunities. My emails to the General Manager went unanswered, while the Regional Manager responded and indicated that member feedback could help influence decisions regarding staffing and operating hours. We apply this policy consistently to every member, without exceptions. Pros:
+ Pretty good hours (late nights and weekends). Though the showers close 30min before the publicized hours so if you actually stay late you'll be forced to shower at home.
+ A lot of squat racks (~8+)
+ Equipment itself is high quality and there are a full range of machines.
+ Large footprint (square footage)
+ Good variety of exercise classes included
+ Mobile App is solid compared to most gyms
+ Good location
+ Staff is very friendly (though limited) and available to answer questions which is great. Other gyms don't answer the phone.
+ Not really crowded (at least on weekends and late evenings so I haven't experienced waiting for equipment)
+ Rainfall showers, sauna, hot tub are nice.

Cons:
- Trash:  Way too much trash strewn about. e.g Men's locker room bins overflowing, small scraps of paper, gum wrappers,  used chap stick left behind, razor blade caps (left in showers), clothing tags, etc. I've reported this to the management on at least 2 occasions with no improvement. Part of this is on the guests/members for not being as considerate but regardless of fault it impacts the experience really negatively. This is especially in my experience closer to the end of the day, which feels understaffed.  Uploaded some photos (but it's so common you can just come for a tour late evening tomorrow and you'll see it for yourself). I just heard another member this morning complaining in the locker room about "how frustrating it is to see people lift heavy weights then not able to lift the towels or trash to the receptacles."
- Poor maintenance:   Towels consistently overflowing the bins, strewn about in locker room benches. It’s downstairs and definitely not fancy, but they pack a surprising amount of equipment into the space. Lots of free weights, plate-loaded machines, cardio equipment and pretty much everything you need to get a proper workout in. Locker rooms and showers were decent and everything was clean.

We paid $40 per person for a day pass, which I thought was a little steep for what you’re getting, but it was convenient and did the job. It wasn’t overly busy when we were there either, which was a big plus. Staff were friendly and getting the day pass was easy.

If you’re looking for luxury amenities, this probably isn’t the place. I primarily attend the women’s strength classes, and I occasionally take some of the other offerings like co-ed strength + conditioning and restore classes. Even though I had lifted before, I was intimidated to come to my first class. Tight-knit women’s fitness communities can either be incredibly welcoming or feel very cliquey, and Grassroots was such a breath of fresh air from the very beginning.

The community is warm, supportive, and genuinely encouraging - not cliquey at all. Seasoned members are always helping newer members learn the ropes, and everyone really does cheer each other on. It is the kind of place where people notice your progress and celebrate your wins.

The coaches are somehow able to balance teaching new members while still challenging seasoned members, without making anyone feel held back or left behind. There is clearly a science and method to their magic, but they make it look effortless. I can promise you there is so much thought that goes into the workout formula for every class.

What really sets Grassroots apart is how intentional they are about teaching proper form, technique, and the “why” behind each movement. The 6-week “off-the-bar” series is a perfect example — it is designed to build the skills and body awareness needed to perform better during the 8-week “on-the-bar” series. Instead of just pushing you to sweat or lift heavier, the coaches help you understand what each movement is doing, what you should be focusing on, and how to move in a way that supports your body.

I had gone to a different lifting gym years ago and often felt like I was constantly getting injured or chasing a good workout without really understanding my body. Grassroots has been completely different. I feel stronger, more confident, and much more connected to how my body works.

And on top of all of that, it is genuinely fun. The space is beautiful, the equipment is top-notch, the music is great, the teachers bring such good energy, and even the swag is fun. It feels like a place you actually want to show up to, not a place you have to drag yourself to.

They also offer resources like InBody scans, and they take the time to walk you through what every part of the scan means — not just the number on the scale. That level of education and support has helped me feel like I’m finally taking my power back.

Grassroots is more than just a gym. Before starting at X93 almost 3 years ago I was told that I needed a full knee replacement surgery. My knees were locking, unstable, and limiting what I could do day-to-day. Chris took the time to understand my specific challenges and designed a strength program that safely rebuilt the muscles supporting my knees. Over time, my pain decreased, my stability improved, and I regained confidence in my movement. Thanks to his expertise and careful coaching, I’ve been able to avoid knee replacement surgery — something I honestly didn’t think would be possible.

Beyond my knees, my overall body strength has increased dramatically. I’m stronger, and more balanced. Chris emphasizes proper form, functional strength, and sustainable progress. Every workout is intentional, challenging, and tailored to help you improve safely.

The true proof of how effective this training has been came recently when I had a fall coming down the steps of an airplane overseas. It was one of those moments that could have easily resulted in a serious injury. Instead, I was able to catch myself and walk away with only stitches on my leg. In that moment, I realized just how much strength training has protected me. The stability, muscle strength, and body awareness I’ve developed at X93 made all the difference.

Chris is knowledgeable, encouraging, and genuinely invested in his clients..The gym is immaculately clean and he and Anthony have succeeded in attracting a friendly and diverse clientele who help make the often dreaded and hard workout much less painful.

[{"Name":"Bunker Blake","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjV0KqL08NtbdFuSxGHzHJtby8pXF4iZSG8DWaajOm_p5bJYzsfP=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"I first started training at Hanson Fitness in 2010 when they were still on Greene Street. I was working a demanding finance job in Midtown and trying to reclaim the athleticism I’d lost after years of focusing on school, my career, and a healthy amount of partying.

At the time, I was already running and taking cycling classes, but I realized I needed to learn proper strength training. I used part of my first meaningful bonus to hire a trainer and ended up becoming a client for roughly a decade.

My first trainer was Eric K., and over the years I also worked with Clive M., Omar V., Eric E., Kirk F., Eugene, Hank, and Liz. Every trainer was different, but all were knowledgeable, professional, and genuinely enjoyable to be around. There were others I worked with episodically over the years, and while I can’t remember every name after all this time, I remember appreciating what each of them brought to the experience.

Harry Hanson deserves special recognition. Despite operating multiple studios downtown, he remained remarkably hands-on. He knew his clients, knew his trainers, and showed up. In an industry full of trends and constant reinvention, Hanson Fitness remained independent and owner-operated for more than three decades, which I find deeply admirable.

Equally important was the gym’s commitment to education. Harry built and ran a formal trainer development program, creating a culture in which coaching and learning were taken seriously. It gave the gym a different energy than most transactional fitness businesses.

When Hanson later moved to its current location, it felt like a meaningful milestone. The new space was a clear upgrade and a sign that the business had real momentum. For longtime clients, it felt less like a relocation and more like validation of everything Harry and his team had been building for years.

For me, Hanson became the foundation underneath everything else I did. During the same period, I took more than 1,000 group fitness classes, ran marathons, and played hockey at Chelsea Piers. Hanson was where I built the strength, mobility, and durability that supported it all. The stronger legs, shoulders, back, and glutes I developed there paid dividends for years.

Convenience was another major advantage. The location was ideal for anyone living below Washington Square Park. My sessions started at 6:00 a.m., and some of my favorite memories are of arriving while the city was still asleep. Before the emails, meetings, and deadlines began, a handful of people quietly prepared for the day ahead.

What stands out most in retrospect is the mix of people. This is SoHo, and personal training isn’t cheap, but Hanson somehow maintained a welcoming, grounded atmosphere. There were young professionals, retirees, entrepreneurs, executives, and people from every imaginable background all training together.

Looking back, Hanson felt like part of the invisible backbone of New York. Many people there were doing demanding work across finance, law, healthcare, technology, media, and entrepreneurship. At six in the morning, titles and money didn’t matter much. Everyone was just trying to get stronger, feel better, manage stress, and keep going. When I was younger, I assumed places like Hanson were common. With time, I realized they’re not. Hanson somehow humanized a city that is far more fragmented and isolating than it first appears. It brought together people from different industries, generations, and walks of life who otherwise might never have known one another.

Fitness is a vain, fickle, and trend-driven business. Through all of that, Hanson remained focused on the fundamentals: coaching people effectively, helping them get stronger physically and mentally, and building a sustainable business. The fact that it has endured for more than three decades in New York is not an accident.

Fifteen years later, I still use lessons I learned there. In an industry full of trends and constant reinvention, Hanson Fitness remained independent and owner-operated for more than three decades, which I find deeply admirable.

Equally important was the gym’s commitment to education. Harry built and ran a formal trainer development program, creating a culture in which coaching and learning were taken seriously. It gave the gym a different energy than most transactional fitness businesses.

When Hanson later moved to its current location, it felt like a meaningful milestone. The new space was a clear upgrade and a sign that the business had real momentum. For longtime clients, it felt less like a relocation and more like validation of everything Harry and his team had been building for years.

For me, Hanson became the foundation underneath everything else I did. During the same period, I took more than 1,000 group fitness classes, ran marathons, and played hockey at Chelsea Piers. Hanson was where I built the strength, mobility, and durability that supported it all. The stronger legs, shoulders, back, and glutes I developed there paid dividends for years.

Convenience was another major advantage. The location was ideal for anyone living below Washington Square Park. My sessions started at 6:00 a.m., and some of my favorite memories are of arriving while the city was still asleep. Before the emails, meetings, and deadlines began, a handful of people quietly prepared for the day ahead.

What stands out most in retrospect is the mix of people. This is SoHo, and personal training isn’t cheap, but Hanson somehow maintained a welcoming, grounded atmosphere. There were young professionals, retirees, entrepreneurs, executives, and people from every imaginable background all training together.

Looking back, Hanson felt like part of the invisible backbone of New York. Many people there were doing demanding work across finance, law, healthcare, technology, media, and entrepreneurship. At six in the morning, titles and money didn’t matter much. Everyone was just trying to get stronger, feel better, manage stress, and keep going. When I was younger, I assumed places like Hanson were common. With time, I realized they’re not. Hanson somehow humanized a city that is far more fragmented and isolating than it first appears. It brought together people from different industries, generations, and walks of life who otherwise might never have known one another.

Fitness is a vain, fickle, and trend-driven business. Through all of that, Hanson remained focused on the fundamentals: coaching people effectively, helping them get stronger physically and mentally, and building a sustainable business. The fact that it has endured for more than three decades in New York is not an accident.

Fifteen years later, I still use lessons I learned there. [{"Name":"Emilia Castaing","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjUZUrE9cXh-a-A7mfpJUslMAkm4D-YyemzcrYrLeYVUqwoPb3g=s120-c-rp-mo-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"Joining that very first class was one of the best decisions I’ve made. Once you discover Jungle Body, there is no way back! Every class hypes you up and recharges your energy in a way that not many things can. Yin and all the JB babes know how to bring a good and effective workout that makes you sweat a lot, but feels like clubbing because everything happens in a room with nightclub lighting. We are always moving through the music, and sometimes the classes are with a live DJ as well, so it’s even more like a party.

The music is always the best, a bit of everything in every class. Attending classes actually expanded my music taste a lot because they really play a wide variety of styles. They also include dance steps from many different dance styles and mix them with boxing, cardio, and workout exercises, always following the music and having the best time—connecting with each other, laughing, and moving nonstop for 45 minutes. (Bring a towel couse you will sweat) Every week there are new routines and new dance steps to so you never get bored and it’s always a challenge.

I’d also like to mention something that I think kind of differentiates Jungle Body from other fitness groups or dance classes: every class has a different dress code, so we can all match! I don’t know, I feel like when we are all matching, the vibe, it’s different haha.

The vibe you’ll find is very high energy, mainly women, and very diverse. there are always people from everywhere. I’m personally from Chile, and I always find someone new to speak Spanish with in class haha. Yin, the main instructor, has an Asian background. I remember Pam is from the Philippines, Marion is from France, and all the backgrounds you can think about. There isn’t really an age range either; there are people of all ages. Some could be my granny, and sometimes kids come when Mimi, Yin’s wonderful, energetic, fun, talented, high-presence daughter comes and sometimes invites friends. So yeah anyone is welcome in class.

If you’re thinking of joining, don’t think twice because the first class is free—that’s how I started. I was just where the class was because I was taking a dance class before, and the energy of the people arriving caught my attention from a distance. I couldn’t resist going to ask what was going on that people were so excited about, and yeah… it makes sense that it was this.

I’m so grateful to Yin and all the Jungle Body team for making me feel welcome when I was new in Australia. They became my safe space and support system naturally and very quickly when I had no one else. It’s very special how no one goes unnoticed. It’s not like other dance or fitness classes where you pay, take the choreo or do the workout, everyone minds their own business, and leaves. Here, there is a lot of chatting, or even when there’s no time to talk because you’re dancing and moving, you exchange smiles with more than one person in the room and hear a few “hey,” “let’s go,” “c’mon,” “get it girl,” and lots of yells and screams hyping everyone up, coming from any of the JB babes who are always at the front keeping the energy high.

I’m so proud of what Jungle Body is now and what it’s becoming, because like everything, at first it was just a dream—Yin’s dream. no air-conditioning. especially upstairs is appalling. it's somehow hotter inside than it is outside on some days. not to mention, the bathrooms consistently have a foul odour from what i assume is a ventilation issue.

the lower bathrooms lost their sanitation dispensers for wiping the seats for some reason.

a personal nitpick others might be fine with are the newly installed spotlights. they create an aesthetic well lit interior for promotional material but functionally, when you're working out and being blasted with a spotlight, it can be a distracting and unpleasent experience.

the most significant beneficial changes are the amenities/services added such as powerbanks, juice machine, massage areas, etc. but even these are either a paid add on or there to sell a product.

I could go on and on...

It's clear anytime used this renovation as an excuse to increase the price without properly evaluating the facilities or functionality of the gym. its a sloppy coat of paint so they can sell what on the outside may look like a "premium" gym.

$30 A WEEK is the price for a gym I find to be in the top 3 worst that i've experienced.

This is one of the better Anytime Fitness locations I’ve visited. The gym is surprisingly large for the brand and is extremely well-equipped, with a strong focus on strength training. Whether you’re training chest, back, legs, shoulders, or delts, you’ll find plenty of equipment options available. There are four power racks, two Smith machines, and an impressive cable setup that makes it easy to train almost any muscle group without having to wait long for specific equipment.

One thing that stands out is the variety and depth of equipment. Even during busy periods, it’s rare to find yourself unable to train a particular body part because there are usually alternative machines or stations available. The gym also has plenty of toilet and changing facilities, which is always appreciated.

The main downside is the crowd. No matter what time I visited—even late at night—the gym was consistently busy. I suspect the nearby university contributes to the younger crowd and steady foot traffic throughout the day. While most equipment is well distributed, the leg press machines seem to be permanently occupied, so expect a wait if leg day is on the agenda.

Overall, a fantastic Anytime Fitness location with excellent equipment selection, plenty of training options, and good facilities. What is most concerning is not a single maintenance issue or one-off closure—it’s the constant pattern of members paying premium prices while being repeatedly denied access to the facilities and amenities included in their membership.

The pool, spa and sauna area has become a perfect example. Last Saturday, the entire area was closed for the day because the club was understaffed. Today, the area was closed again well before the advertised closing time. The spa has also been unavailable for extended periods over the past six months due to renovations, broken pipes and other maintenance issues. Altogether, I estimate it has been out of service for well over a month during that period.

Even when the wellness area is open, staff have increasingly started cleaning and applying slippery chemicals up to 45 minutes before closing, despite the area officially remaining open to members. Guests are effectively being pushed out early because management has chosen operational convenience over member experience.

The gym floor itself is not much better. The upstairs cable fly machine has broken down repeatedly, multiple cardio machines are frequently out of service, and members are constantly dealing with construction works and restricted access to facilities. The climbing wall is being removed and replaced with office space, creating ongoing disruption, and now renovation works have extended onto the gym floor itself, with sections of the weights area blocked off during peak evening hours.

The Pilates studio air conditioning was also unreliable for an extended period, making classes uncomfortable and, at times, difficult to attend.

What makes all of this particularly frustrating is that membership fees continue to increase while the overall member experience continues to deteriorate. Equipment breaks down repeatedly, amenities are unavailable, facilities are closed due to staffing shortages, and construction works seem never-ending. Yet members continue to be charged premium prices for a service that is increasingly falling short of a premium standard.

I fully appreciate that maintenance, repairs and upgrades are sometimes necessary. However, the sheer volume of recurring issues points to a broader management problem rather than isolated incidents. There appears to be a lack of planning, accountability and operational oversight.

The staff on the floor are generally friendly and helpful, but they can only work with the resources and direction they’re given. The responsibility for the current state of the club sits with management.

I would welcome a response from senior or national management because, unfortunately, the examples above are only a portion of the issues members have been dealing with throughout the year. Virgin Active Pitt Street has enormous potential, but right now it is failing to deliver the premium experience that members are paying for.","Images":["https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/grass-cs/ACvplmOM0lz00tAgO0Dz6eryPMarSbu0V1nkuZLC1tASlNSBfsE02Cw2XbbhIpLplq3cSEwDmASE-VeClB26izc06ve5wp7lojLY_O276xkPV6yYswAnch_wzGaIz5sHGMhMopi751KinUWczQRO=k-no","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/grass-cs/ACvplmOLTN2R19qcrMnAFDR7w_h5igO6OPC2AI6d9O-wxNvdQVQezap2y7de4wpFZ0lBsqmoFv9YLpvq9T_NKmC_DV1R2pimryrkb5l-OhfJ-s01vAdb5Nxj8OxqqwOCzs6fs_KYu1DiJ_usomT-=k-no","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/grass-cs/ACvplmOXNieNnhzBh8fWKFaUgqyzoIlRcj2DG41yajb6N28WBZ5jQISnimKfs_i3QWOOeqs28ZUYKZdtQEaflWD0MpclHrEHl01SKIWiSRSD9Nv0WzFXtlnR08A242p5uS3h2--dw8btJPOx-NF5=k-no","https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/grass-cs/ACvplmOsw2KpvGHbna4HDczUzCathlZ1OGfvvAwVRbVpQNo0ecSdzZM36FjeZ6OgLqFrZRPfezpThOmNCGDlm4YyDTSt3Ka2w9sqW_sYM82hCkN23_xCzNwdTs_0YvVxM9MNPf7ZZWmKBqxHrPs=k-no"],"When":"2 months ago","review_id":"Ci9DQUlRQUNvZENodHljRjlvT2psdk1qZzRNV3c1V1dWTk5tVkdSV1o2UldVM1lsRRAB","source":"Google","rating_scale":5,"rating_float":2,"author_url":"https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/101128568016208249168/reviews?hl=en-GB","posted_at_unix_micros":1782211585544424,"updated_at_unix_micros":1782211585544424,"language":"en","translated_lang":"","text_original":"I’ve been a member of Virgin Active Pitt Street for almost three years, and I can honestly say that the club is currently being managed worse than at any point since I joined.

Most of the squash coaches are friendly, respectful, and professional, including Anna, Shayaz, and many others. The squash court bookings and courses are also affordable, which is one of the reasons I enjoyed coming here. That is why, like many other members, I used to come more often on Tuesday evenings after work. It is also one of the most popular times for people working in the city who want to play squash after work. Unfortunately, these amazing coaches either left for uni / internship / etc. or only attend Saturday classes.

However, I had a very bad experience with one coach, Leigh Sands, during the Tuesday evening squash classes. I only attended his class twice, but both experiences were enough to make me avoid Tuesday classes and eventually cancel my membership.

From the first class, I felt he was targeting me rather than simply coaching me. At first, I tried to give him the benefit of the doubt and thought maybe that was just his teaching style. But after the second class at 5:45pm on 28 April 2026, it became very clear to me that his behaviour was rude, disrespectful, and unacceptable.

I completely understand that safety is important in squash. I respected Leigh’s instruction when he told me to knock before entering the court, even after the play had finished. However, when other members did the same thing in the same class, he said nothing. That made the situation feel a bit strange but still not so alarming to me.

What upset me most was not the safety instruction itself, but the way he communicated. There are many respectful ways to speak to an adult member. Instead, Leigh shouted at me and told me to get out of the court in front of other members. People in the court looked shocked by his behaviour.

I tried my best to follow his instructions in both classes, even though I already felt he was being rude and disrespectful. I do not know why he treated me this way. As someone who is recently quiet and experiencing bereavement, I cannot help but feel that I may have been singled out because of my quietness. I truly hope I am wrong, but his behaviour made me feel bullied and disrespected.

Leigh Sands may be a good squash player, but based on my experience, he is not a good coach or communicator. A coach should not shout at members or humiliate them in front of others.

The experience with his both classes is the reason I am cancelling my membership. It is disappointing because I genuinely liked Hiscoes and many of the people there. However, this kind of behaviour should not be ignored. I have been attending Clarence Street Snap Fitness and the space lacks cleanliness and is sadly filthy. Gym is meant to bring health and positive aspects to our life.

I was a previous member at Snap fitness in Perth, where the situation was very different and have moved to Sydney in the last 2 weeks. The Clarence Street location was the most convenient for me to attend.

I tried to the manager (whom is hardly ever at the reception desk and only found exercising) as to work with improvements for a filthy environment is unacceptable.

The gym has no soaps in most of the toilet sinks, stations where wipes are located is super dirty around… the other day there was not a single alcohol gel bottle filled to be used. Dust is everywhere especially weight sections. This week the stair climber equipment has a spider web right in front, with a spider hanging there.

The manager asked me to send him an e-mail yesterday, which I did. I wrote and included pictures as to the matter.  I wasn´t comfortable with the fact that I had already spoken and no one else was in copy as to address the issue. The manager replied to my e-mail on the same day, informing those actions would be taken, but on the following day I was surprised with an unexpected incident today towards me.

Today, I was surprised with a rude approach from one member, which and opted not to reply and continued with my music and exercise. I didn´t respond and wished the man “all the best” when we left the gym at the same time. Latter that day the same manager sent me an e-mail filled with lies as if I was the one with inappropriate behavior in the gym, when I was the one who received an unexpected attitude when returning the man´s towel.  The manager wrote that I had inappropriate behavior at the gym, to members and staff members. That I was no longer welcome at the gym. This is a lie and didn´t occurred at all!!

I am surprises and shocked with these two incidents which apparently might be connected… I felt so unsafe today. I was the only women and was mistreated and later received an email filled with lies. I only wanted to use one of the 3 benches, which 2 were being used and the third was occupied by his towel. I decided to wait and do another exercise. While I was doing a rep of 4x18, the man that left his towel at the beach only came once. Once I was finished, I literally went to him and ask if I could use the equipment. He said yes. Which was great. I had music on my ears and grab his towel to give it back to him. OMG! That guy, freaked out, he was so arrogant, saying he could grab the towel himself and that I was rude to touch his towel. He kept speaking rudely towards me (I felt harassed). That was just awful! I felt so mistreated by the tone of his voice and the way he kept speaking to me. I said I didn’t hear him and didn’t know it was rude to give the towel back to him. Afterward I only said: “you’re a very rude man, and I’m glad I’m not listening to you, as I have headphones on”. It was awful, really. I felt terrible and didn’t feel safe at all.
